newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $10 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $10 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 lower Wednesday on the heels of a weak performance in London, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures slumped in thin turnover early Wednesday. At the midday break, May was down six stg at 1,019 stg a tonne, while July fell eight stg to 1,034 stg.

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures ended weaker in uneventful dealings, with dealers continuing to focus on the May/July switch. May cocoa closed down $4 at $1,414 a tonne, toward the floor of its $1,413 to $1,427 range. Most-active July eased $6 to $1,455.
May's discount to second-month July traded out to $44 yesterday before pulling back to $41 at the close, down from $43 Monday.
Traders expect the narrowing of the switch to continue over the next few days, as dealers roll shorts forward ahead of May delivery period on April 17.
Technically, good support was seen for July at Friday's low of $1,433. To the upside, a large chart gap awaited at $1,480 to 1,504. ((-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
